title.zh: 一张没有抓到人的警网
title.en: A Net That Caught No One

dek.zh: 皇帝下令搜捕一个并不存在的妖党首领，抓不到人的巡抚接连挨骂。一位被人叫作「老菩萨」的老巡抚，要怎样回话？
dek.en: The emperor wanted a sorcerer chief who did not exist, and one provincial governor after another was scolded for failing to catch him. How was an aging governor, known as "the Old Bodhisattva," supposed to reply?

paras.zh: 1768年6月中旬，叫魂的谣言传进了江西。它走的是江西东面的信江河谷，那是通往邻省浙江的一条便捷通道。江西巡抚吴绍诗年约七十。谣言已经进了他的辖境，他没有向朝廷奏报。
paras.en: In the middle of June 1768, rumours of soulstealing reached Jiangxi. They came through the Xin River valley on Jiangxi's eastern side, the easy route into the neighbouring province of Zhejiang. The governor of Jiangxi, Wu Shaoshi, was about seventy. The rumours had entered his jurisdiction, and he sent no report to the court.

paras.zh: 这一年，乾隆皇帝弘历追究各地官员为何抓不到妖党首犯。研究这场风波的历史学家孔飞力指出，皇帝的怒气可以发在没抓到首犯的地方官身上，而这种失职躲不开，因为这样的妖首并不存在。孔飞力也强调，弘历当时并没有察觉这个案子的荒谬。巡抚们面对的，是一位认真追究的皇帝，和一个抓不到的目标。
paras.en: That year the Qianlong emperor, Hongli, pressed provincial officials over their failure to catch the sorcerers' leaders. Philip A. Kuhn, the historian who reconstructed the panic, points out that the emperor could turn his anger on provincial officials who failed to catch those leaders. They could not avoid failing, because no such leader existed. Kuhn also insists that Hongli did not see the absurdity of the case at the time. The governors faced an emperor who was in earnest about the hunt, and a quarry that could not be caught.

paras.zh: 先看别省的巡抚是怎么回话的。河南巡抚阿思哈向弘历解释，术士们有隐身的秘术，所以逃脱了。弘历在朱批里嘲笑他：你心里存着这种想法，难怪属下缉拿不力，他们是在欺你这个「无用废物」。替抓不到人找理由，换来的是皇帝的嘲骂。
paras.en: Consider first how governors elsewhere answered. Asiha, the governor of Henan, explained to Hongli that the sorcerers had escaped because they knew a secret art of making themselves invisible. Hongli answered in a rescript, the comment the emperor wrote in vermilion ink on an official's report. He mocked Asiha: with ideas like that in his head, no wonder his subordinates were slack about arrests, since they were taking him for a "useless good-for-nothing." Offering an excuse for catching no one only brought the emperor's ridicule.

paras.zh: 浙江巡抚冯钤走的是另一条路。他报告说，已让省臬司去调查妖术嫌犯。孔飞力说，寻常情况下这本是很合理的做法。弘历却斥他推诿卸责，先是一句反问：「此何等事，而汝按例交臬司？」意思是，这是什么样的事，你竟照常例交给臬司？接着问他难道不该每天亲自详细审讯，最后下了结论：「外省习气实在可恶！」照规矩办事，在这件案子里也成了罪过。
paras.en: Feng Qian, the governor of Zhejiang, took a different line. He reported that he had handed the investigation of the suspects to the province's judicial commissioner. Kuhn notes that in ordinary circumstances this would have been an entirely reasonable step. Hongli instead accused Feng Qian of shirking. He opened with a rhetorical question: "What sort of matter is this, that you hand it to the judicial commissioner according to routine?" He then asked whether Feng Qian ought not to be conducting detailed interrogations in person every day, and closed with a verdict: "The habits of the provinces are truly detestable!" In this case even going by the rules counted as an offence.

heading.en: What the Old Bodhisattva Sent In

paras.zh: 吴绍诗的处境和他们不太一样。叫魂危机的前一年，有人告诉弘历，江西巡抚吴绍诗被人唤作「老菩萨」。孔飞力写道，弘历很担心这位老菩萨太消极无为，耽误公事。吴绍诗的健康也有问题。弘历为此去问两江总督高晋。高晋是吴绍诗的顶头上司，也是弘历的姻亲。他说没听说有什么事能证明吴绍诗不称职，并答应继续观察、随后报告。弘历相信吴绍诗经验丰富、诚实可靠，让他留任。
paras.en: Wu Shaoshi's position was not quite like theirs. The year before the crisis, someone told Hongli that people called the governor of Jiangxi "the Old Bodhisattva." Kuhn writes that the emperor worried this Old Bodhisattva was too passive and might let official business slide. Wu Shaoshi's health was also in question. Hongli asked Gao Jin about it. Gao Jin was governor-general of Liangjiang, Wu Shaoshi's immediate superior, and a relative of the emperor by marriage. He replied that he had heard of nothing showing that Wu Shaoshi was unfit for office, and he promised to keep watching and report later. Hongli believed Wu Shaoshi to be experienced, honest and dependable, and kept him in his post.

paras.zh: 此外，弘历对吴绍诗的家族也十分尊重：吴绍诗是一个著名法律世家的大家长。按照回避原则，同一家族的成员通常不许同时在这样的衙门任职，但吴绍诗和他的儿子吴焕、吴坛，曾两次被同时任命在刑部供职。
paras.en: Hongli also held Wu Shaoshi's family in high regard. Wu Shaoshi headed a celebrated family of legal experts. Under the rule of avoidance, members of one family were normally barred from serving in the same government office at the same time. Even so, Wu Shaoshi and his sons Wu Huan and Wu Tan were twice appointed together to the Board of Punishments, the central ministry of justice.

paras.zh: 回到6月。谣言入境，吴绍诗没有奏报。他后来向弘历报告说，自己曾口头命令属下留意可疑的行旅。但江西没有人被捕，省内也没有发现剪辫的事。对他不奏报谣言，弘历只是温和地驳斥他：「汝误矣」，意思是你做错了。孔飞力说，弘历对这位年高誉隆的巡抚表现出了出乎意料的克制。
paras.en: Back to June. The rumours had crossed the border, and Wu Shaoshi sent no report. He later told Hongli that he had verbally ordered his subordinates to keep an eye on suspicious travellers. But no one was arrested, and no cases of queue-clipping turned up in the province. On the failure to report the rumours, the emperor rebuked him only mildly: "You were wrong." Kuhn calls it an unexpected show of restraint toward an elderly and highly respected governor.

paras.zh: 吴绍诗的次子吴坛是邻省江苏的按察使，和父亲一样是受人尊敬的法律学者。他的情形与父亲不同：他没有向朝廷报告的，是江苏当年春天实际发生的叫魂案件。织造萨载把叫魂案密报上去，吴坛因此蒙羞。吴坛承认自己未及时报告，弘历在朱批里先提他过去的表现：「汝在刑部时，表现出色。然一任外省，即染模棱腐败之陋习。」意思是你在刑部时干得很好，一到地方就染上了含糊敷衍、腐败的毛病。最后骂他是「不知恩之物」，不知感恩的东西。父亲得到一句「汝误矣」，儿子挨了一通痛骂。
paras.en: Wu Shaoshi's second son, Wu Tan, was judicial commissioner of neighbouring Jiangsu. Like his father he was a respected legal scholar. His case was different, though: what he failed to report to the court were actual soulstealing cases in Jiangsu that spring. Then Sazai, the imperial textile commissioner, sent a secret report on the cases, and Wu Tan was disgraced. When Wu Tan admitted that he had failed to report in time, Hongli's rescript began with his past record: "When you were at the Board of Punishments, you performed splendidly. But as soon as you took a provincial post, you caught the vile habits of equivocation and corruption." It ended by calling him an "ungrateful creature." The father received "You were wrong" and the son a torrent of abuse.

paras.zh: 到了10月初，吴绍诗交上一份很不一样的报告。他说自己在省内布下了一张比任何别省都严密的警网：挑选干员「改装易姓」，换了装束、改了姓名，分赴各县秘密查缉，每旬报告一次有无可疑人物；又令各府州派精细强干的人，去查访「庵观寺院祠堂书馆及深山密箐等处」，查访范围从寺庙道观、祠堂书馆，一直到深山密林。
paras.en: In early October, Wu Shaoshi sent in a very different kind of report. He said he had spread a net across his province tighter than any other province's. He had picked capable agents who would "change their dress and take other surnames," so that they could travel in disguise and search each county in secret, with a report every ten days on whether anyone suspicious had appeared. He had also ordered each prefecture and department to send sharp, able men to search "convents, temples and monasteries, ancestral halls, schools, and deep mountains and dense thickets." The places named ran from religious houses and ancestral halls to the remotest forest.

paras.zh: 吴绍诗的奏报里还有一段警告。他说那些从事「左道邪术」的人，借创立烧香好善会的名义，「阳则聚集乡愚男妇，阴则勾结亡命棍徒」，明面上聚集乡间男女，暗地里勾结亡命之徒；又借避灾防盗之名，造作妖言、制备军器、诱人归附。他要求不论僧道还是其他人，凡是面生可疑、神气沮丧、迁徙无定、怕见人的，都要立即报告地方官。弘历的朱批是：「恐属空言，实难信矣口」，恐怕只是空话，实在难以相信。这是一句明白的怀疑。
paras.en: In his memorials Wu Shaoshi also issued a warning. Practitioners of "heterodox ways and evil arts," he wrote, set up incense-burning charitable societies as a front, "openly gathering ignorant village men and women, secretly colluding with desperadoes and ruffians." On the pretext of warding off disaster and bandits, they spread wicked talk, stockpiled weapons and drew people into their following. He ordered that anyone, monk, Daoist priest or layman, who was an unfamiliar face, looked dejected, kept moving from place to place, or avoided being seen, be reported to the local officials at once. Hongli's rescript read: "I fear these are empty words; truly hard to believe." It was open doubt.

paras.zh: 此后，江西确实什么事也没有发生。六个星期以后，弘历已经中止了清剿，吴绍诗在一再谦卑地谢罪之后报告说，江西没有发现一起剪辫案。孔飞力说，没有档案文字能证明江西曾像邻省那样搜捕过可疑嫌犯。
paras.en: And indeed nothing happened in Jiangxi. Six weeks later, after Hongli had already called off the campaign, Wu Shaoshi apologized humbly and repeatedly and then reported that not a single case of queue-clipping had been found in the province. Kuhn notes that no archival document shows Jiangxi ever rounding up suspects as the neighbouring provinces did.

paras.zh: 吴坛走的是另一条路。挨骂大约三个星期后，约9月28日，他奏报说，虽然没有抓到叫魂案犯，但查访发现苏州城外有十一座由俗人建造的佛教经堂。随后约七十人被他逮捕，供词显示这些教派从1677年起就在当地活动。孔飞力自己说明无法证实，但他推测：这种规模的教派在苏州这样繁忙的城市不可能长期瞒过官府；按察使受到抓人的压力，压向属下，底层经办人员便拿这些无事而易欺的信徒来交差。弘历的反应十分严厉，下令严惩这些教徒，并审问他们与叫魂案的联系。经堂案又牵出一轮追责，受罚名单从知县一直排到总督，但大多数人只受到象征性处罚，孔飞力称之为一幕闹剧。
paras.en: Wu Tan went another way. Around September 28, about three weeks after the emperor's tirade, he reported that he had caught no soulstealers, but his inquiries had uncovered eleven Buddhist scripture halls outside Suzhou, built by lay believers. He then arrested about seventy people, and their confessions showed that the sects had been active in the area since 1677. Kuhn says plainly that he cannot prove it, but he conjectures that sects of this size could not have stayed hidden from the authorities for long in a city as busy as Suzhou. In his reading, the judicial commissioner was under pressure to make arrests and passed it down to his subordinates, and the clerks and runners at the bottom handed over these harmless, easily bullied believers to have something to show for their efforts. Hongli reacted very severely. He ordered the sectarians harshly punished and had them questioned about any links to the soulstealing. The scripture-hall case then set off a round of punishments for past officials, with names ranging from county magistrates up to governors-general, though most received only token penalties. Kuhn calls the impeachment process a farce.

paras.zh: 叫魂案收场时，孔飞力写道，弘历以在官僚中寻找替罪羊来结束清剿，要借处罚失职官员表明他的清剿是正确的。被单独挑出来重罚的是苏尔德。叫魂案在苏州刚发生时，他在任上却没有陈奏；后来做山西巡抚，又「清剿阻挠尤甚」，也就是阻挠清剿最厉害。弘历把他贬为省按察使，发往新疆。吴绍诗则安然度过了这场危机：弘历不但没有斥责他，第二年还任命他为刑部尚书。
paras.en: When the soulstealing affair ended, Kuhn writes, Hongli brought the campaign to a close by looking for scapegoats among his officials, and he meant to show, by punishing their failures, that his campaign had been right. The official singled out for heavy punishment was Su'erde. He had been serving in Suzhou when the first cases broke out there and had not reported them. Later, as governor of Shanxi, he "obstructed the suppression most of all." Hongli demoted him to provincial judicial commissioner and sent him off to Xinjiang. Wu Shaoshi, by contrast, came through the crisis unharmed. Far from rebuking him, Hongli appointed him president of the Board of Punishments the following year.

paras.zh: 江西到底发生了什么？孔飞力摆出两种可能：要么这张警网从来没有真正动用过，要么它根本捕捉不到嫌犯。他注意到，江西看不到其他省份那种刑求和伪证，于是推断吴绍诗根本不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子，那些忧心忡忡的警告和精心的布置都只是「装模作样」。
paras.en: What actually happened in Jiangxi? Kuhn sets out two possibilities: either the net was never really put to use, or it was incapable of catching anyone. He observes that Jiangxi shows none of the torture and false testimony found in other provinces, and from this he concludes that Wu Shaoshi never intended to pursue a case he believed rested on false rumour. In Kuhn's view, the anxious warnings and the elaborate deployment were only a performance.

paras.zh: 如果采纳孔飞力的推断，本文作者推断，“表面配合、实际不动”能够成立，是几件事凑在了一起。一是形式：交上去的正是皇帝要的东西，有部署、有查访地点、有定期汇报，连警告都用的是清剿自己的语言。二是时机：那份查无一案的报告，是在清剿中止之后、伴着谢罪交上去的。三是人：七十岁的年纪、法律世家的声望、弘历留任他时的信任，还有既是顶头上司又是皇帝姻亲的高晋。孔飞力对他安然无恙的解释也落在人上：因为他的法律造诣，也可能因为高晋的袒护，要惩罚他「不愿加入这场集体游戏」并不容易。
paras.en: If Kuhn's inference is accepted, I would argue that several things came together to let outward compliance and inward inaction succeed. The first was form. Wu Shaoshi sent in exactly what the emperor wanted: a deployment, named places to search, regular reports, even warnings phrased in the campaign's own language. The second was timing. The report that nothing had been found arrived after the campaign had been halted, wrapped in apologies. The third was the man himself: his seventy years, his family's reputation in the law, the trust the emperor showed in keeping him on, and Gao Jin, his immediate superior and the emperor's relative by marriage. Kuhn's own explanation of why Wu Shaoshi escaped also turns on the man. Because of his legal expertise, and perhaps because Gao Jin protected him, it was not easy to punish him for declining to join in what Kuhn calls a collective game.

paras.zh: 风险同样有记录可查。弘历在吴绍诗的这段警告上批了「恐属空言」；「老菩萨」的名声和消极误事的担心，危机前一年就摆在了皇帝面前；苏尔德的下场则说明，清剿收场时弘历要在官员中找替罪羊，不报和阻挠的人可能被单独挑出来重罚。本文作者推断，吴绍诗躲过去，很大程度上靠的是别人借不来的条件，同样的做法换一个人，换来的可能是另一种朱批。
paras.en: The risks are on record too. Hongli wrote "I fear these are empty words" in response to Wu Shaoshi's warning. The Old Bodhisattva nickname, and the worry that he was too passive, had reached the emperor a year before the crisis. Su'erde's fate shows that when the campaign ended and Hongli looked for scapegoats among his officials, those who had failed to report or had obstructed the campaign could be singled out for heavy punishment. My inference is that Wu Shaoshi got through largely on advantages no one else could borrow. Another official doing the same thing might have received a very different rescript.

paras.zh: 这也不是一个智者对抗暴君的故事。孔飞力列举过官僚抵制的几种情形：有深思熟虑的，有程序颟顸误了时机的，有因不信其事而轻视此案的，有怕清剿危及仕途的，也可能有耿直官员拒绝依据诬告迫害无辜。他说这些行动不像是协调一致的，抵制专制权力并不需要串通。对江西，孔飞力的推断是，吴绍诗“根本就不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子”。本文作者认为，这最接近因不信其事而轻视此案的一种。孔飞力也提醒，说弘历“利用”了政治罪，并不比说政治罪“利用”了他更接近真实。本文作者的一种解读是，江西的平静和苏州的七十人被捕，都出自同一套结构，差别在于每个官员怎样接住同一份压力。
paras.en: Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Some came from sluggish procedures that kept officials from reacting to an emergency in time. Some officials, doubting the whole thing, may have refused to take the cases seriously. Others may have feared that the suppression campaign would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. For Jiangxi, Kuhn infers that Wu Shaoshi never intended to pursue a case he regarded as a false rumour; in my reading this comes closest to the officials who doubted the whole thing. Kuhn also cautions that saying Hongli "used" political crime is no closer to the truth than saying political crime "used" him. My own reading is that the quiet in Jiangxi and the seventy arrests in Suzhou came out of the same structure. What differed was how each official handled the same pressure.

paras.zh: 本文唯一的依据是孔飞力《叫魂》的中译本（陈兼、刘昶译），没有使用其他史源。朱批和奏报都转引自书中译文，与档案原文是否逐字一致无法判断。“只是装模作样”是孔飞力的推断，他先列出过警网根本抓不到人的可能，但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信装模作样的解释；吴绍诗为何难以受罚，孔飞力归于他的法律造诣，并推测可能还有高晋的袒护。高晋答应的后续报告，孔飞力没有找到。
paras.en: This article rests entirely on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers, by Chen Jian and Liu Chang, and uses no other source. The rescripts and memorials are quoted as they appear in that translation, so I cannot tell whether they match the archival originals word for word, and the English renderings here are translations of that Chinese text. The claim that Wu Shaoshi was merely putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Kuhn first named the possibility that the net simply could not catch anyone, but, finding no torture or false testimony in Jiangxi, concluded that only the explanation of a show was credible. As for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Kuhn attributes it to his legal expertise and conjectures that Gao Jin's protection may also have played a part. Kuhn was unable to find the follow-up report Gao Jin promised.

scenario.zh: 总部根据一阵风声发起全面排查，要求各区“限期出成果”，邻区陆续交上了名单。你是一位资深区域负责人，判断这阵风声并不属实，于是交出一份详尽的排查方案，却没有拿人凑数。
scenario.en: Headquarters, acting on a wave of rumour, launches a sweeping investigation and tells every region to deliver results by a deadline. One by one, neighbouring regions hand in lists of names. You are a senior regional head. You judge the rumour to be false, so you submit a detailed investigation plan and do not round up people to fill the quota.

question.zh: 这样做保护了可能被冤枉的人，也可能被总部视为敷衍。你凭什么判断自己能承担这个风险？如果你没有资历和专业声望撑腰，还会这样做吗？
question.en: Your choice protects people who might be wrongly accused, but headquarters may see it as going through the motions. What makes you think you can carry that risk? Would you do the same if you had no seniority or professional reputation to fall back on?

assumptions.zh: 假设这位负责人在总部有专业口碑，直属上级愿意替他说话，但总部已经有人质疑他“只交方案不交结果”。
assumptions.en: Assume this regional head has a strong professional reputation at headquarters and a direct superior willing to speak up for them, but some people at headquarters are already complaining that they deliver plans and no results.

steps.zh:
先确认自己的判断有依据，而不只是直觉：风声来自哪里，有没有可核实的线索。
方案写到可以检查的程度：查了哪些地方、按什么频率汇报、谁负责。
汇报“查无此事”时说明依据，而不是只写结论。
估计最坏结果：如果被认定为敷衍，代价由谁承担，会不会落到下属身上。
steps.en: 1. First make sure the judgment rests on evidence and not just instinct: where did the rumour come from, and are there leads that can be checked? 2. Write the plan in enough detail to be checked: which places were searched, how often reports are made, and who is responsible. 3. When reporting that nothing was found, give the grounds for that finding rather than the conclusion alone. 4. Estimate the worst case: if the work is judged a mere formality, who pays the price, and could it fall on subordinates?

alternative.zh: 本文作者提出的另一种做法：不只是交方案，而是在方案里明确写出自己对风声真实性的判断和理由，请总部给出认定“成果”的标准。这样更透明，但也把分歧摆上了台面，风险可能更早到来。
alternative.en: Another approach, proposed by this article's author: instead of simply submitting a plan, state in it your own judgment of whether the rumour is true and your reasons, and ask headquarters to define what counts as results. This is more transparent, but it also brings the disagreement into the open, and the risk may arrive sooner.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文只依据孔飞力《叫魂》中译本。朱批引文照书中原样，「恐属空言，实难信矣口」中的“口”字照录未改。吴绍诗“装模作样”是孔飞力的推断；他为何难以受罚，孔飞力给出的理由中，高晋的袒护一项是推测。
uncertainty_note.en: This article relies only on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers. Rescripts are rendered from the text as printed there. In that text, the rescript translated here as "I fear these are empty words; truly hard to believe" ends with a stray character (口) that the Chinese article reproduces unchanged, and it is left out of the English translation. The view that Wu Shaoshi was only putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Of the reasons Kuhn gives for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Gao Jin's protection is a conjecture.

preheader.zh: 全国都在抓“叫魂”的妖人，江西巡抚交出一份周密的方案，却一个人也没抓。第二年，他升了官。
preheader.en: While every province hunted 'soul-stealers' in 1768, Jiangxi's governor filed a meticulous plan and arrested no one. The next year he was promoted.
